name: Centro de Meditacao Kadampa Deuachen
aka: Kadampa Temple for World Peace, Sintra
Fourth Kadampa Temple for World Peace

location.address: Rua Moinho do Gato 5, Varzea de Sintra, 2710-661 Sintra

tradition: New Kadampa Tradition (NKT-IKBU), Gelug-derived Modern Kadampa Buddhism
technique: Lamrim-based analytical and placement meditation on lovingkindness, compassion, and emptiness, plus tantric practice and silent retreat, following the teachings of Geshe Kelsang Gyatso
influences: New Kadampa Tradition - International Kadampa Buddhist Union (NKT-IKBU)
teacherAccess: Resident teacher Gen Kelsang Rigden gives regular classes, weekend courses, and retreat teachings; visiting NKT teachers lead festivals and special retreats
retreatOptions: Weekend and multi-day residential retreats held regularly at the temple (including periodic silent retreats and a post-Summer-Festival meditation retreat), with onsite overnight accommodation for one or more nights; day courses and weekly classes also offered
about: Centro de Meditacao Kadampa Deuachen, also known as the Kadampa Temple for World Peace, is a Tibetan Buddhist temple in the Sintra hills west of Lisbon, part of the New Kadampa Tradition - International Kadampa Buddhist Union founded by Geshe Kelsang Gyatso Rinpoche. The temple was consecrated by Geshe Kelsang Gyatso in 2013 and today functions as both a public visitor site, with gardens, a cafe, and a shop open most days, and a residential Dharma center running weekly classes, courses, festivals, and retreats, including periodic weekend and multi-day residential meditation and silence retreats with onsite overnight accommodation. Teachings follow Geshe Kelsang Gyatso's Lamrim (stages of the path) and lojong mind-training texts through the center's General Program, Foundation Program, and Teacher Training Program, led by resident teacher Gen Kelsang Rigden. The community runs largely on volunteers, including a working-guest program offering free room, board, and classes in exchange for daily help around the temple. Meals for volunteers and some retreat guests are ovo-lacto vegetarian, and all proceeds from courses, retreats, and festivals support the NKT's International Temples Project.
schedule: Weekly classes and weekend courses year-round; periodic multi-day residential retreats (e.g. a week-long post-Summer-Festival meditation retreat and dedicated silent retreats); guided temple visits Tuesdays and Thursdays
cost: Pay-per-activity fees for classes, courses, and retreats, plus optional monthly membership cards giving discounted access; accommodation, meals, and transport are priced separately and are not covered by membership cards
foodNotes: The temple cafe serves food to day visitors; working guests and volunteers receive free ovo-lacto vegetarian meals; food arrangements for paying retreat participants vary by program and are booked separately from the teaching fee.
workNotes: Retreat and course participants are not required to work. A separate voluntary working-guest program is available (about 6 hours/day, 5 days a week) in exchange for free lodging, vegetarian meals, and access to classes.
